rationale: bugs_open/216: the coordinator's response-driven recoverable arm re-arms an awaited request (retry_version++, persisted) and then refuses its own replay (RETRY_PAYLOAD_UNAVAILABLE), failing the parent workflow terminal — so an error_recoverable response is terminal, and the retry_version bump it leaves makes the row look retried. Mechanism, read from source and proven by live induction on v1.0.1262 (probe corr b155c554, request cef0a691: retry_version 0->1 at 08:25:21.5635, workflow_failed 4ms later, DB row still holding a valid payload): (1) ClaimAwaitedRequest claims the row with UPDATE ... SET status='processing' WHERE status='waiting' RETURNING <all columns> — the returned row carries request_payload; (2) the error_recoverable switch arm discards that row and handleRecoverableError re-reads via GetAwaitedRequest, whose predicate status IN ('waiting','retrying') excludes the 'processing' status the claim just wrote — the re-read misses by construction; (3) the in-memory fallback can never carry the payload: RequestPayload is json:"-" (bugs_closed/129/RSH-003 — it must never enter the orchestration_states JSONB), and ProcessResponse loads state fresh from the DB on every response (coordinator.go:261), so the fallback is payload-less on EVERY response-driven recoverable, same-pod included; (4) retry_version is persisted, then DecodeRetryPayload("") fails and the workflow is failed terminal. The fix is the bug file's candidate 1, chosen because it closes the door: hand the claimed row (already returned, payload included) through to handleRecoverableError, mirroring the parameter handleCompleteResponse already takes, and delete the doomed re-read and fallback rather than patching their predicates. The claim is exclusive (single-actor guarantee, coordinator.go:283) and nothing writes the row between claim and decide on either path, so no re-read can be fresher than the RETURNING row. CONSUMERS, named per the 2026-07-29 ruling: the two callers of handleRecoverableError. (a) The response path (ProcessResponse switch, coordinator.go:322) — the broken one; ProcessResponse structurally guarantees a non-nil claimed row (nil returns at :252). (b) The timeout retry driver (retryExpiredAwaitedRequest -> :3448), previously healthy because its claim writes 'retrying', which the old predicate included; it now passes the row ClaimAwaitedRequestForRetry returned, which is value-identical to what its re-read used to fetch (RETURNING is post-update; no intervening writes), so its guarantee is unchanged. This fix is the gate on the retry-quality programme's prize: 195/197/207 all deliver INTO this arm, and while it stands every upstream classifier win buys a bookkeeping write instead of a retry (~30% deadline-exceeded census, bugs_open/207). The retry cap (retry_version >= 3) and no-backoff bounds are unchanged (RSH-006). Regression tests included; the discriminating test was mutation-verified (reintroducing the fallback fails it with the filed shape). A 090 diagnosis run on the filing completed with no clean verdict after 5 iterations; its final round's citations independently re-derive the central code fact, and the filing's live induction stands as primary evidence — the verdict read is recorded in the bug file.

plan.summary: handleRecoverableError decides retries on a row it re-reads with a predicate its caller's claim has just made unsatisfiable, then falls back to an in-memory copy that structurally cannot carry the replay payload — so every response-driven recoverable retry is refused after its retry_version bump is persisted. Change handleRecoverableError to take the claimed row from its caller (both callers hold one, returned by their claim's RETURNING with request_payload included), delete the re-read and the fallback, and pass the row at both call sites. Truth up GetAwaitedRequest's doc comment, which cites the removed re-read. Add regression tests that recreate the hostile world (unreachable DB, payload-less in-memory copy) and assert the replay reaches the wire.

edits.rationale: The decision must be made on the row the caller claimed — the RETURNING row is the current DB row, payload included, and the claim is exclusive, so no re-read can be fresher. The re-read misses by construction on the response path ('processing' vs predicate 'waiting','retrying'), and the fallback can never carry a payload (json:"-"), so both are removed rather than patched.

plan.risks: 1) The timeout-driven consumer (retryExpiredAwaitedRequest) previously had a working DB re-read plus a fallback for transient read failures; it now uses the claimed row only. Check: the claim's RETURNING is value-identical to the old successful re-read there, and a path with zero reads has strictly fewer transient failure modes than one with a read plus fallback. 2) Any third caller of handleRecoverableError would need the new parameter — the signature change makes an un-updated caller a compile error, and a grep shows exactly two callers. 3) The renamed log line: nothing in scripts/, docs/ or bugs_*/ parses the old literal ('Using in-memory awaited request' appears only as quoted evidence in bugs_open/216). 4) The refusal guard (bugs_closed/129) must not weaken: a payload-less claimed row still refuses — asserted by the second test. 5) Retry cap and no-backoff bounds unchanged (retry_version >= 3, RSH-006): fixing this arm widens the live retry population to what 197/207 already promised, no further.
